items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: I was with him four and a half years... So I took it as an apprenticeship for four years... So for four and a half years I was under his armpit.

ctx.x: Tell us about playing with one of the absolute masters of jazz, an institution within himself. Tell us about Art Blakey.

Yeah, he was, when I was with him first of all, I was with him four and a half years and so I just hung out with him. I didn’t try to tell him nothing. You know I see a lot of young kids, they don’t know how to keep their mouth shut, you know? That’s the biggest thing you’ve got to learn how to do is keep your ears open and your mouth shut. You know? Ears open, mouth shut. And that’s what I did with Art. And he appreciated that. If Art asked me my opinion on something, I would give it. He’d say “what do you think…

this, Bobby?” Well I think this— But I never try to tell him anything of my own personal experiences, because I figured what can I tell him? He’s played with Bird and everybody, and so there was nothing that I was going to tell him, my experiences aren’t relevant to this man. And if he wants to know — the only thing that’s relevant to this man is my performance on the bandstand and for me trying to be the best Jazz Messenger I can be and to make sure that he’s happy. So I took it as an apprenticeship for four…
